jobs.description:
What to Expect

The Tesla Robotics Team designs and builds humanoid bi-pedal robots (Optimus) to perform tasks that are boring, repetitive, and dangerous for humans. As a CAE Engineer, you will guide the design of sensors and structural components using high-fidelity FE models grounded in sound engineering principles Working closely with mechanical, electrical, controls, software, and manufacturing teams, you’ll analyze and optimize designs, challenge traditional CAE methods, and pioneer more efficient, accurate approaches. This role places you at the forefront of critical design and engineering decisions, shaping a robust and reliable humanoid robot that has never been executed before.

What You’ll Do

- Develop and analyze comprehensive Finite Element (FE) models for Optimus, from individual components to the full system
- Conduct static, dynamic, structural and MBD simulations to evaluate and validate the performance against key requirements for strength, stiffness, durability and sensing
- Build and refine simulation workflows to assess performance across diverse operating scenarios, automate processes, documentation, and tools to improve efficiency, accuracy, and repeatability
- Provide design guidance to world-class engineering teams, enabling data-driven product decisions
- Collaborate with Test Engineering to design and validate experiments, correlate test data with simulations, and enhance predictive modeling capabilities
- Establish and maintain modeling standards, methods, and best practices for current and future programs
- Material characterization and advanced modeling of structural and sensing components
- Plan and execute large-scale DOEs, creating ML driven surrogate models to extract insights to drive key design decisions

What You’ll Bring

- Degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience
- Strong foundation in Engineering Mechanics, Computational Mechanics, Material Science, and Finite Element Theory and applications
- Demonstrated ability to guide structural, sensing, thermal, and mechanism designs through CAE, from concept to mass production, across robotics, automotive, and consumer electronics
- Expertise in building high-fidelity FE models at component, sub-system, and full-system levels
- Proficiency in linear and non-linear static, dynamic and modal simulations and experience developing multi-physics simulation workflows (e.g., thermal-mechanical, mechanical-electrical)
- Advanced knowledge in material characterization and modeling, including nonlinear elasticity, viscoelasticity, creep, and strain-rate dependent plasticity in Metals, Plastics, Polymers and Adhesives
- Proficiency in CAE Tools such as BETA CAE, LS-DYNA, Abaqus, ADAMS, COMSOL, OPTISTRUCT, Design Life, FE Safe
- Strong programming and data analysis skills in MATLAB, Python, or equivalent
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams
- Ability to communicate at a professional level in English language, both verbally and written
- Ability to travel internationally on a regular basis

We work with the cross-functional teams (Design, Quality, Production, Sustaining, and Supply Chain) throughout the entire lifecycle of a product (from initial design through prototype development and into full production) to develop volume manufacturable designs and processes that will produce gearboxes. The role of the Gearbox Manufacturing Engineer is to support gearbox manufacturing process development to produce world-class gearbox prototypes and drive scalable production methods to high volume production. jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description:
Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,500 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com
The Position
As Lead Human Pharma Public & Government Affairs Obesity and Metabolic Health you will join a dynamic team dedicated to engaging with policymakers around the world to enable the access and uptake of life-changing pharmaceutical innovation. As part of the Public & Government Affairs function in the Corporate Affairs division, you will deliver integrated campaigns to drive meaningful policy change in particular areas of healthcare. At this time, we especially welcome applications from candidates with experience in policy shaping focused on Obesity and Metabolic Health, the therapeutic focus can shift in role based on business need.
This position is based at our Global Headquarters in Ingelheim, Germany.
Tasks & responsibilities

- As the Public & Government Affairs Lead for Obesity and Metabolic Health, in alignment with colleagues in the Corporate Affairs division, you will ensure we develop and implement integrated campaigns. In support of our established portfolio and future launches, you will establish alliances for awareness raising and targeted policy prioritization.
- One of your key tasks will be policy and stakeholder mapping to ensure the company has an informed position for key therapeutic areas within the Human Pharma business. You will lead on the creation of clear policy positions and support wider evidence generation to enable global and country teams to engage with policymakers.
- You will enable Public & Government Affairs capabilities and execution with a particular focus on the EU5, US, China and Japan.
- Moreover, you will support the Head of HP Public & Government Affairs to coach country teams in the development of clear strategic and tactical plans with measurable policy outcomes.
- You will be the main contact person for assigned Therapeutic Areas and other partners in the Human Pharma business. You will provide clear strategic counsel and be recognized as an expert in international health policy and country-level policy change.
- You will establish strong cross-functional relationships with teams including Communications, Market Access, Medical, Marketing, Legal and Compliance.

Requirements

- Master's degree in politics, Health Policy, Sciences, Economics, Law, or equivalent experience
- Several years of experience in a Public & Government Affairs role, potentially in-house, a consultancy or directly in Government
- Deep understanding of healthcare policymaking at a national and global level, including the role of the pharmaceutical sector in general and linked to specific therapeutic areas
- Business know-how to succeed in a global, matrixed organization, able to lead without direct management responsibility
- Demonstrable experience of delivering integrated campaigns to drive meaningful policy change
- Extensive experience in external networking to build meaningful relationships that drive (policy) change
- A true Thearapy Area policy leader with a co-creative mindset and the ability to build trust across the business
- Experience of ensuring successful delivery in line with the Legal and Compliance requirements in the pharmaceutical industry
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills with fluency in English (additional languages are a plus)

With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.

Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.

Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.

Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

Shape the future of manufacturing at Kelvion in Herne as an Operational Excellence Engineer and drive real, measurable improvements across our operations. You will identify and implement optimization opportunities using Lean, Continuous Improvement, and Operational Excellence methods such as 5S, Value Stream Mapping, Kaizen, Root Cause Analysis, and Gemba Walks. - Lead Operational Excellence projects independently in close cooperation with all departments, including savings identification and cost analysis.
- Integrate improvements into daily operations with a strong shopfloor focus and ensure sustainable implementation.
- Moderate workshops and cross‑functional initiatives, and train and coach employees in OPX methods and tools.
- Perform value‑stream analyses, derive action plans, and report project progress, savings, and OPX successes.
- Collaborate across sites to create synergies and foster a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.

Attractive Offer & Environment

- Competitive salary package with attractive benefits, reflecting your expertise and contribution.
- Work in a growth‑oriented industry with strong demand for energy‑efficient and industrial solutions, offering long‑term job security and career development opportunities.
- Join a diverse, international team where different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences are valued. We are committed to an inclusive workplace and welcome applications from all qualified candidates regardless of gender, age, nationality, or other personal characteristics.

Your Background

- Degree in Engineering, Business, Production Technology, or a comparable field.
- At least 3 years of experience in Lean, Continuous Improvement, or Operational Excellence in an industrial environment.
- Solid knowledge of Lean tools and methods (Six Sigma a plus); strong MS Office skills and basic ERP experience.
- Experience with tools such as MS Planner, Visio, Lucidchart, or Power BI is an advantage.
- Excellent communication skills in English and German, team‑oriented mindset, hands‑on attitude, and strong analytical and solution‑driven thinking.

Join Kelvion in Herne and help us build a more efficient, agile, and sustainable production environment on a global scale. We look forward to hearing from you!

Ultrasonic Acoustic Engineer (m/f/d)

Sound Propagation, Resonance & Biofouling Prevention

HASYTEC (Ultrasonic Tech GmbH, part of the ERMA TECH Group) develops and markets highly innovative ultrasonic technology that prevents biofouling on fluid-carrying surfaces. Our systems protect more than 300 ships, offshore platforms, and maritime installations worldwide against barnacles, algae, and mussels—efficiently, sustainably, and with minimal maintenance.

To strengthen our development team, we are looking for an Ultrasonic Acoustics Engineer who is passionate about understanding sound propagation, resonance behaviour and ultrasonic systems in complex maritime structures.

You will help develop the next generation of ultrasonic anti-fouling technology.

Our long-term goal is to protect not only piping systems and sea water equipment, but also large ship hull structures through controlled ultrasonic resonance fields.

Your responsibilities include:

- Analyze ultrasonic wave propagation in maritime structures and materials
- Investigate resonance behaviour in piping systems, sea chests, strainers, box coolers, propeller systems and hull structures
- Develop and optimize ultrasonic transducer configurations and installation concepts
- Plan, execute and evaluate laboratory experiments and onboard vessel trials
- Measure vibration behaviour and acoustic transmission using modern test equipment
- Analyze experimental data and derive practical design improvements
- Collaborate with hardware, software and mechanical engineering teams
- Coordinate technical activities with universities and research institutes

Technical Qualifications

- Degree in Physics, Acoustics, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics or a related field
- Experience in one or more of the following: - Ultrasonics
- Acoustics
- Vibration analysis
- Resonance behaviour
- Signal processing
- Experimental testing
- Experience with laboratory measurement equipment such as oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers or vibration measurement systems
- Experience in data analysis using Python, MATLAB or similar tools
- Experience in maritime systems, fluid-carrying structures or piezoelectric technology is beneficial but not required
- Analytical and systematic working style
- Curiosity for understanding physical phenomena
- Hands-on mentality and enthusiasm for experimental work
- Ability to bridge theory and practical application
- Team-oriented mindset and initiative
- Our working language is English

What Makes This Role Unique

This is not a standard engineering position.

You will work on challenging acoustic problems involving sound propagation, structural resonance and ultrasonic excitation in real maritime applications.

The role combines physics, experimentation, onboard testing and collaboration with leading research institutions to develop sustainable technologies for the maritime industry.

What we Offer

- Work with a unique technology that contributes to more sustainable shipping
- A combination of laboratory research, practical testing and real-world applications
- High levels of responsibility and influence within a growing company at the forefront of sustainable technology
- Collaboration with international customers, universities and research institutes
- Modern equipment and short decision-making processes
- A technically strong and motivated, multi-professional international team
- employee benefits such as corporate pension schemes, bikeleasing and more

Postdocs (2 years) (m,f,x)

The Cluster of Excellence "CASA: Securing the Digital Society" is funded by DFG for the years 2026-2032 with approximately 53 million euros. CASA aims to strengthen the resilience of our digital society. The emergence of disruptive technologies in recent years, especially artificial intelligence and quantum computers, has caused substantial new challenges for cybersecurity research. In the second funding phase, CASA will specifically address these challenges. Thematic priorities include the security of quantum technologies, protection against Al-based disinformation and societal polarization, and new approaches to defending against ransomware. In addition to technical questions, it also investigates the interaction of human behavior and cybersecurity. Research at CASA, which is based at the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security, follows a strongly interdisciplinary approach. Researchers from the fields of computerscience, cryptography, electrical engineering, mathematics, and psychology work together in an unique constellation in Europe. This holistic approach is unparalleled and holds the potential for scientific breakthroughs. Ruhr-University Bochum (RUB) and its Faculty of Computer Science offer an excellent environment for aspiring young researchers. 20 years ago, the Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security (HGI) was founded here. lt is now one of Europe's most prestigious institutions for basic computer security research. The HGI maintains extensive networks with leading research institutions worldwide and with media and industry. Moreover, it has produced numerous successful security startups. The pioneering work of the HGI forms the basis for the Cluster of Excellence CASA.

Scope: full-time
Duration: fixed-term, 2 years
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-11-09

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Theoretical Condensed Matter Physics (three years) (m/f/x) (Physiker/in)
jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (29.8725 hours/week = 75%;) by 12-2026, we are looking for one

PhD Position in Theoretical Condensed Matter Physics (three years) (m/f/x)

The Research Group of Prof. Ilya M. Eremin at Theoretical Physics III at Ruhr University Bochum conducts research on the theory of quantum materials, with a particular focus on strongly correlated electron systems, unconventional superconductivity, magnetism, and collective phenomena. Our research aims at developing a microscopic understanding of emergent electronic phases in quantum materials and their experimentally observable signatures. A central focus of our current research is the physics of unconventional superconductors and correlated quantum materials, including recently discovered nickelate superconductors. These systems provide a particularly rich platform in which electronic correlations, orbital degrees of freedom, magnetism, structural effects, and superconductivity are intimately intertwined. Understanding their phase diagrams and excitation spectra requires the development and application of advanced many-body theoretical approaches.

One PhD position in Theoretical Condensed Matter Physics is available in the Research Group Theoretical Physics III at Ruhr University Bochum. The successful candidate will investigate microscopic mechanisms of unconventional superconductivity and competing electronic phases in strongly correlated quantum materials. Particular emphasis will be placed on multiorbital systems such as bilayer and multilayer nickelates, although related problems in cuprates and other unconventional superconductors may also be addressed. The project will combine analytical and numerical many-body techniques, including tight-binding and multiorbital models, Green's-function methods, mean-field and Bogoliubov–de Gennes approaches, and methods for treating electronic correlations and collective excitations. Depending on the specific research direction and the candidate's interests, functional renormalization group, slave-boson/Gutzwiller approaches, random-phase approximation, and numerical calculations of experimentally measurable response functions may also be employed. An important aspect of the project will be the close connection between microscopic theory and current experiments, including spectroscopy, transport, and scattering measurements. The PhD researcher will work in an active international research environment and interact closely with theoretical and experimental collaborators in Germany and abroad.

Scope: part-time
Duration: fixed-term, 3 Jahre
Start: by 12-2026
Apply by:  2026-10-05

Your tasks:

- Development and investigation of microscopic theoretical models for strongly correlated quantum materials and unconventional superconductors.
- Study of superconductivity, magnetism, density-wave states, and competing or intertwined electronic orders in multiorbital systems.
- Analytical and numerical calculation of electronic structures, superconducting gap functions, collective excitations, and experimentally accessible response functions.
- Development and application of advanced many-body methods, depending on the specific research problem.
- Comparison of theoretical predictions with experimental results from spectroscopy, transport, and scattering experiments.
- Development, implementation, and documentation of numerical codes for theoretical calculations.
- Close collaboration with other members of the research group and with national and international theoretical and experimental partners.
- Presentation of research results at national and international conferences, workshops, and scientific meetings.
- Publication of the results in international peer-reviewed scientific journals.

Your profile:

- A successfully completed university degree (Master's degree or equivalent) in physics, with a strong background in theoretical physics.
- Very good knowledge of quantum mechanics and solid-state physics.
- A strong interest in condensed matter theory, quantum many-body physics, and unconventional superconductivity.
- Previous knowledge of many-body theory, superconductivity, magnetism, strongly correlated systems, or quantum field theoretical methods is advantageous.
- Experience with numerical calculations and scientific programming, for example in Python, C/C++, Julia, Mathematica, or comparable environments, is desirable.
- Candidates should be motivated to develop and apply analytical as well as numerical theoretical methods.
- Ability to work independently and reliably while contributing actively to collaborative research projects.
- Good communication skills and willingness to work in an international and interdisciplinary research environment.
- Good command of written and spoken English is expected.

IT System Administrator (m/f/d) with a focus on Network & Database

Compugraphics Jena GmbH is a subsidiary of Element Solutions Inc. As a leading manufacturer of precision components for the microelectronics industry, we offer a wide range of microtechnology services, including the development, production, and optimization of components.

We place great emphasis on quality, innovation, and customer satisfaction, and maintain strict quality control processes to ensure that all products meet the highest standards.

The aim of the position is to ensure stable, secure and efficient IT operations through the professional support and further development of the IT infrastructure, especially in the areas of system administration, networks and database management

Tasks and Responsibilities

- User management and assignment of rights in Active Directory
- Installation, configuration and maintenance of Windows and Linux systems
- Monitoring and maintenance of the server landscape (Windows & Linux)
- Support network infrastructure (switches, routers, firewalls) under guidance of IT network team.
- Endpoint setup and management and enrolment of corporate PCs (via script, Intune and ManageEngine)
- Support and further development of our FileMaker databases with necessary change management.
- Planning and execution of backups and disaster recovery
- Patch and update management for operating systems and applications
- Support and training of employees in IT matters
- Documentation of IT infrastructure and systems
- Implementation of security systems/updates/policies under guidance of IT security.
- Inventory management of hardware and software
- Performance monitoring of productive database systems
- Plan and execute system migrations and upgrades
- Coordination of external service providers if required
- Support for IT projects and the introduction of new systems
- Manage IT tickets and ensure timely closure of incidents and requests

Requirements ad Qualifications

- Completed training in the IT sector (e.g. IT specialist in system integration) or comparable qualification
- Sound knowledge of Windows and Linux system administration
- Experience with Active Directory and User Management
- Good knowledge of network technology (switches, VLAN, firewalls, routing)
- Experience with endpoint management (ideally Microsoft Intune and ManageEngine)
- Basic knowledge of database management – FileMaker is particularly advantageous
- Experience with backup and recovery solutions
- Structured, independent and solution-oriented way of working
- High sense of responsibility and ability to work in a team
- Very good written and spoken German, Good English
- Experience with Telephony support (Mobile and PBX) 
- Experience of an ITSM system for IT Tickets, Change Requests etc.
- ITIL Foundation preferred
